Maya (PM): Quick sync — we need to align on the long-term routing + multi-tenant isolation roadmap for the next 3 quarters. I sketched a proposed priority list below. Please react with :thumbsup: if you agree and drop any quick blockers.

Proposed priorities (starting highest):
1) Policy DSL & guardrails (canary hooks, RBAC, validation)
2) Tenant affinity lanes (soft/hard affinity, quota plumbing)
3) Cross-region failover & bandwidth contracts (RTO/RPO, egress controls)
4) Migration automation (sandbox -> prod, cutover tooling)
5) Routing observability & routing decision telemetry

Primary asks to resolve here: launch gates per initiative, customer-driven asks that bump priority, minimal-risk migration path, and initial cost estimate for pilots.

Raj (Eng-Arch): SGTM. We must quantify acceptance criteria. For Policy DSL: require per-route SLOs, canary hooks, schema validation, and an RBAC surface. Also: implement staged rollout API.

Aisha (Product): FYI — two regulated customers asked specifically for per-tenant egress & data residency as a gating item. That pushes cross-region/residency higher for enterprise segments.

Luca (Platform): Noted. Affinity lanes increase cluster fragmentation and cost. Need a migration cost delta estimate (monthly) and a pilot capacity plan before we greenlight.

Elena (SRE): We need a runbook for cross-region failover. Define RTO target (suggest 5 min for control plane; 99th pct request failover within 30s) and a playbook for tenant quarantine.

Ben (Sales): Sales signal: 2 enterprise prospects require traffic isolation SLA + private deployment timeline. If we can commit to a beta in Q3, it'll help closing.

Maya (PM): Proposed launch gates for each initiative (draft):
- Gate A: End-to-end canary (traffic slice + automated verification)
- Gate B: Perf within 15% of baseline tail-latency and throughput SLOs
- Gate C: Automated rollback + fallback policy tested in canary
- Gate D: Runbooks, runbook drills, and SRE on-call assignment
- Gate E: Customer migration checklist + legal/contract signoffs (for residency)

Raj (Eng-Arch): Telemetry we should capture from day one: routing_decision_latency, fallback_rate, tenant_isolation_errors, kv-cache_miss_rate, routing_policy_eval_time. Those let us measure safety & perf regressions.

Aisha (Product): Add migration UX items: opt-in migration windows, pause/resume, customer-visible fallback notices. Those are a legal ask for some customers.

Luca (Platform): Suggest pilot strategy: 3 pilot tenants — 1 internal, 1 low-volume customer, 1 enterprise. Call it "isolation-lane-0". Estimate: +20% peak cluster overhead for soft affinity; +40% for hard isolation. Will confirm with infra.

Elena (SRE): Oncall impact: initial pilots can be handled by rotating oncall if runbook exists; we should add an escalation path to platform owners. Also recommend synthetic traffic tests for canary.

Maya (PM): Can we get a rough estimate (cost + infra risk + ETA) by EOD Friday? @Raj @Luca please. If not EOD, put a quick note with open assumptions.

Raj (Eng-Arch): I'll post a short engineering guesstimate tomorrow morning. Quick note: model-aware routing is a technical risk — large KV caches make live failover lossy. That affects fallback policy design.

Aisha (Product): We must include a quality-preserving fallback: prefer model variants that maintain context where possible. If not possible, surface a degraded-quality notice to the customer.

Luca (Platform): I'll sync with finance and ops for a ballpark cost and timeline and share before Friday EOD. We can also draft a minimal pilot infra spec.

Elena (SRE): I'll draft a runbook template and a list of synthetic tests (latency, error-rate, fallback correctness).

Maya (PM): Great. If no major objections, I'll draft a PRD with three tracks (policy DSL, affinity lanes, region failover) and include these launch gates + telemetry. Planning to schedule 30m working sessions for each track next week. :calendar:

Ben (Sales): Sales to compile target customers and expected commitments, will post them here by EOD Thursday.

Raj (Eng-Arch): One more tech flag: autoscaling + affinity interplay — autoscaler needs tenant-awareness to avoid noisy-neighbor throttles. We'll need an API for capacity hints.

Aisha (Product): Add 'capacity-hints' to the migration checklist and API wishlist. Also require legal review for data residency templates.

Maya (PM): Noted. Action items:
- Raj: engineering guesstimate + tech risk summary (tomorrow)
- Luca: infra cost estimate + pilot spec (Fri EOD)
- Elena: runbook + synthetic test list (Thu)
- Ben: sales customer list + commitments (Thu EOD)
- Aisha: capture enterprise legal/contract asks (Thu)
